q: What is the primary function of a firewall?
opts: Network traffic filtering
Malware detection
Encryption
Password management
exp: Firewall filters network traffic to prevent unauthorized access

q: Which of the following is an example of a phishing attack?
opts: Social engineering
SQL injection
Cross-site scripting
Buffer overflow
exp: Phishing attack tricks users into revealing sensitive information

q: What is the purpose of a honeypot in computer security?
opts: To deceive attackers into revealing their identity
To detect and prevent network attacks
To encrypt sensitive data
To monitor system performance
exp: Honeypot deceives attackers into revealing their identity

q: Which of the following is an example of a zero-day exploit?
opts: Malware that exploits a previously unknown vulnerability
A firewall that filters all incoming traffic
A password manager that stores sensitive data
A secure protocol that encrypts data
exp: Zero-day exploit takes advantage of previously unknown vulnerability

q: What is the term for the process of verifying the identity of a user or system?
opts: Authentication
Authorization
Encryption
Decryption
exp: Authentication verifies the identity of a user or system

q: Which of the following is an example of a denial-of-service (DoS) attack?
opts: Malware that steals sensitive data
A network attack that overwhelms a system with traffic
A password manager that stores sensitive data
A secure protocol that encrypts data
exp: DoS attack overwhelms a system with traffic

q: What is the purpose of a digital signature in computer security?
opts: To encrypt sensitive data
To authenticate the sender of a message
To verify the integrity of a message
To detect and prevent network attacks
exp: Digital signature verifies the integrity of a message

q: Which of the following is an example of a man-in-the-middle (MitM) attack?
opts: Malware that steals sensitive data
A network attack that intercepts communication between two parties
A password manager that stores sensitive data
A secure protocol that encrypts data
exp: MitM attack intercepts communication between two parties

q: What is the term for the process of encrypting data to protect it from unauthorized access?
opts: Encryption
Decryption
Authentication
Authorization
exp: Encryption protects data from unauthorized access

q: Which of the following is an example of a Trojan horse in computer security?
opts: Malware that steals sensitive data
A network attack that overwhelms a system with traffic
A program that appears harmless but contains malicious code
A secure protocol that encrypts data
exp: Trojan horse contains malicious code that appears harmless

q: What is the purpose of a secure socket layer (SSL) certificate?
opts: To encrypt sensitive data
To authenticate the sender of a message
To verify the integrity of a message
To detect and prevent network attacks

q: Which of the following is an example of a buffer overflow attack?
opts: Malware that steals sensitive data
A network attack that overwhelms a system with traffic
A program that appears harmless but contains malicious code
A secure protocol that encrypts data
exp: Buffer overflow attack overflows a system's memory

q: What is the term for the process of detecting and preventing network attacks?
opts: Intrusion detection
Intrusion prevention
Encryption
Decryption
exp: Intrusion prevention detects and prevents network attacks

q: Which of the following is an example of a cross-site scripting (XSS) attack?
opts: Malware that steals sensitive data
A network attack that intercepts communication between two parties
A program that appears harmless but contains malicious code
A secure protocol that encrypts data
exp: XSS attack injects malicious code into a website

q: What is the purpose of a key exchange protocol in computer security?
opts: To encrypt sensitive data
To authenticate the sender of a message
To verify the integrity of a message
To establish a secure connection between two parties
exp: Key exchange protocol establishes a secure connection between two parties
